ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Measuring routing consistency of image latent patches in DiT-MoE
PROPOSAL: We train DiT-B/2 with token-choice MoE layers of eight experts on ImageNet at 256 resolution and record, for every latent patch, the expert chosen at each layer across denoising timesteps, across neighbouring patches, and across samples of the same class. We compute routing entropy, the mutual information between expert choice and timestep, spatial position and class, and the overlap of expert token sets, and we repeat the same analysis on a language MoE of similar size trained on text to compare how concentrated the routing is.
CONTROLS: A dense DiT-B/2 with the same activated parameters, the same MoE with a fixed random router, DiffMoE-style batch-level routing, and expert-choice routing, all trained for the same number of samples and scored by FID and sFID with the same sampler.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Routing of image patches should be far less consistent than for text tokens, with most mutual information on timestep and position and little on content. If the random router matches the learned one in FID, the learned router carries no specialisation at all.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Timestep and frequency conditioned routing for diffusion transformers
PROPOSAL: We design a router that receives, besides the token, an embedding of the denoising timestep and the local spatial-frequency energy of the patch, and that assigns tokens to experts through a two-level choice: first a group by noise level, then an expert within the group by content. We train DiT-L/2 with eight experts on ImageNet at 256 resolution, matching the activated parameters of the dense model, and we measure expert specialisation as the consistency of expert assignment for the same patch across adjacent timesteps and as the divergence between expert input distributions.
CONTROLS: Dense DiT-L/2 with matched activated parameters and with matched total parameters, token-choice DiT-MoE, expert-choice EC-DiT and DiffMoE, all trained under the same schedule and sampler, plus the two-level router with the content level replaced by a random choice.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The conditioned router should beat token-choice routing in FID and show far higher assignment consistency. If the random content level does as well, specialisation comes only from the noise-level grouping.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling experts and model size under a specialisation-promoting router
PROPOSAL: We test whether a router trained with an auxiliary loss that rewards non-overlapping expert inputs keeps improving over dense DiTs as the model and the number of experts grow. The loss pushes apart the mean input features of different experts and penalises tokens whose top two expert scores are close. We train DiT-S/2, DiT-B/2 and DiT-L/2 with four, eight and sixteen experts on ImageNet at 256 resolution, with activated parameters held equal to each dense model, and report FID, sFID and precision and recall at each point of the grid.
CONTROLS: Dense models at each size, token-choice routing with the standard load-balancing loss only, expert-choice routing, a random fixed router, and all variants trained for equal numbers of samples with the same sampler and guidance scale.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The gap over dense should widen with model size and expert count for the specialisation loss, while token-choice routing should stay flat or shrink. If the random router scales equally well, capacity rather than routing explains the gains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert specialisation measured through input-distribution divergence
PROPOSAL: We define specialisation as the average pairwise divergence between the distributions of token features received by different experts, estimated by a classifier that tries to tell which expert a token went to, and we compute it for DiT-MoE, EC-DiT and DiffMoE trained on ImageNet at 256 resolution with DiT-B/2 backbones, as well as for a language MoE trained on a text corpus. We then correlate specialisation with FID gain over dense across checkpoints and layers to test whether specialisation predicts image quality.
CONTROLS: A dense DiT-B/2, each MoE with a random fixed router as the zero-specialisation reference, and a shuffled-assignment version of the classifier test as its chance level, with all diffusion models trained under one schedule and sampler.
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: Specialisation should be low for all three image routers compared with the language model and should correlate positively with FID gain across checkpoints. If specialisation rises without FID improving, the metric does not capture what matters for generation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Patch-level semantic density and its effect on expert routing
PROPOSAL: We hypothesise that latent image patches carry too little distinct content per token for routers to separate them, and we test it by changing the tokenisation: we train DiT-B/2 MoE models with patch sizes of two, four and eight latent pixels and with a learned token merger that groups similar neighbouring patches before routing. For each, we measure routing entropy per token, the mutual information between expert choice and a pretrained semantic label of the patch, and FID against the dense model at equal activated parameters, on ImageNet at 256 resolution.
CONTROLS: Dense DiT-B/2 at each patch size, token-choice routing without merging, expert-choice routing, a random router, and a language MoE whose tokens we artificially merge to the same degree, all under one training schedule and sampler.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Larger or merged tokens should raise semantic mutual information and improve the MoE gain over dense, up to the point where resolution loss dominates. If routing entropy stays flat across patch sizes, token density is not the limiting factor.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spatially coherent routing with neighbourhood-pooled router inputs
PROPOSAL: We feed the router not the single token but a pooled feature over its spatial neighbourhood and the timestep embedding, so that nearby patches of a continuous latent choose experts together, and we add a loss that rewards agreement between adjacent patches' assignments. We train DiT-B/2 and DiT-L/2 with eight experts on ImageNet at 256 resolution and hold activated parameters equal to the dense models. We measure FID, sFID, the spatial coherence of assignments, and the consistency of each patch's expert across timesteps.
CONTROLS: Dense DiT-B/2 and DiT-L/2, token-choice DiT-MoE, EC-DiT and DiffMoE under the same schedule and sampler, the pooled router without the agreement loss, and a random router with spatially coherent but content-free assignments.
COST: 2800
PREDICTION: Coherent routing should reduce FID below token-choice routing and reach a clear gain over dense at both sizes, with the gain larger at DiT-L/2. If the content-free coherent router performs as well, coherence alone and not content drives the gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dense-to-MoE upcycling with expert initialisation from feature clusters
PROPOSAL: We start from a trained dense DiT-XL/2 and convert each feed-forward block into eight experts initialised from the dense weights, but we initialise the router from k-means centroids of token features recorded from the dense model at several timesteps, so that experts start with distinct input regions. We continue training on ImageNet at 256 resolution with activated parameters equal to the dense model and track whether the initial partition persists or collapses, through the overlap of expert input sets over training and the FID gap to the dense model.
CONTROLS: Upcycling with a randomly initialised router, token-choice DiT-MoE trained from scratch for the same total samples, expert-choice routing, the dense model continued for the same steps, and centroids computed on shuffled features as a placebo, all with the same sampler and guidance scale.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Cluster-initialised routers should keep their partition and beat the dense continuation in FID, while random routers should drift towards uniform assignments. If the shuffled-centroid placebo does equally well, the initial partition does not matter.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Routing on denoising-direction features rather than noisy input tokens
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-B/2 MoE models whose router reads, instead of the noisy latent token, the token's predicted clean estimate from the previous block or a lightweight auxiliary head, on the hypothesis that noise in the input token masks the content a router needs. Compare routers fed the raw token, the predicted clean token, and both, with eight experts and activated parameters equal to dense DiT-B/2, on ImageNet at 256 resolution, and measure FID, sFID, routing entropy and mutual information between expert choice and a pretrained semantic label of the patch.
CONTROLS: Dense DiT-B/2, token-choice DiT-MoE, EC-DiT and DiffMoE under one schedule, a random router, and the clean-token router evaluated at high and low noise levels separately to see where it helps, all with the same sampler.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: The clean-estimate router should show higher semantic mutual information and a lower FID than the raw-token router, with most of the gain at high noise levels. If the gain is absent at low noise, the raw token is already informative there.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing token geometry of language and diffusion transformers for routing
PROPOSAL: We extract token features at the input of feed-forward blocks from a trained dense DiT-XL/2 across timesteps and from a language transformer of comparable depth, and we compare their geometry: effective rank, cluster separability under k-means, nearest-neighbour label agreement with semantic labels, and the stability of a token's cluster across timesteps. We then train small MoE layers on frozen features of each kind as a probe of how separable experts become, and we relate the geometry measures to the FID gain of DiT-MoE over dense at DiT-B/2 scale on ImageNet at 256 resolution.
CONTROLS: Features from random-initialised networks as a reference for geometry, dense DiT-B/2, DiT-MoE and EC-DiT trained under one schedule and sampler, and features at a single timestep against features pooled over timesteps.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: Diffusion features should show lower cluster separability and lower stability across timesteps than language features, and the layers where separability is highest should be where MoE gains most. If geometry does not predict the gain, the explanation lies in the router's training dynamics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Load balancing versus specialisation in diffusion transformer experts
PROPOSAL: We test whether the standard load-balancing loss, borrowed from language MoE, is what prevents experts in DiTs from specialising. We train DiT-B/2 with eight experts and token-choice routing on ImageNet at 256 resolution with the balancing weight swept across a range down to zero, with a capacity-based alternative that drops tokens instead of penalising imbalance, and with a loss that balances only within each timestep bucket. We measure FID, expert utilisation, the overlap of expert input sets and the consistency of assignments across timesteps, keeping activated parameters equal to the dense model.
CONTROLS: Dense DiT-B/2, EC-DiT and DiffMoE under the same schedule and sampler, a random router at each balancing weight, and three seeds for the two extreme weights.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Lower balancing weights should raise specialisation and FID gain until expert collapse sets in, and per-timestep balancing should keep utilisation high without harming specialisation. If FID is flat across weights, balancing is not the obstacle.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Timestep-aware routing for class-conditional MoE diffusion transformers
PROPOSAL: Insert a mixture of eight experts into every second block of a DiT-B backbone and route each patch with a learned router that sees the token feature together with the timestep embedding. Train on ImageNet latents at 256 resolution with AdamW, a batch of 256, and a load-balancing term. Generate 50000 samples with the same sampler and guidance scale, and report FID and Inception Score. Also log which experts each patch selects, grouped by noise level and spatial position.
CONTROLS: Compare against a dense DiT with the same activated parameters and the same training steps. Compare against the published token-choice router and expert-choice router with the same number of experts. Measure expert specialization as the mutual information between expert choice and spatial token position, repeated per layer. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Expect a lower FID than the dense DiT-B and a clearer dependence of expert choice on noise level. The claim is refuted if the gain over the token-choice router vanishes across seeds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sparse feed-forward experts selected by noise level and patch content
PROPOSAL: Replace the feed-forward layer of alternate blocks in a DiT-B backbone with eight experts, and let a learned router pick among them using the patch feature plus the timestep embedding. Training runs on ImageNet latents at 256 resolution with AdamW, a batch of 256, and an auxiliary load-balancing term. Sample 50000 images with one sampler and one guidance scale, then report FID and Inception Score, and record expert selections by noise level and patch location.
CONTROLS: Compare against a dense DiT with the same total parameters and the same training steps. Compare against the published timestep-range routing and a round-robin router with the same number of experts. Measure expert load balance as the variance of tokens per expert, repeated per layer. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Expect a lower FID than the dense DiT-B and a more even load across experts. The claim is refuted if the gain over the timestep-range routing vanishes across seeds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Measuring how visual tokens differ from text tokens for routing
PROPOSAL: Quantify how visual tokens differ from text tokens for routing: embed ImageNet patch tokens from a DiT-B and word tokens from a language model, and compute pairwise cosine similarity and clustering structure at each layer. Then train a mixture of sixteen experts whose router takes a neighbourhood-pooled token feature, so that patches with near-identical content reach the same expert. Optimise with AdamW and a batch of 256, FID on 50000 ImageNet samples at 256 resolution is reported, and relate it to the measured overlap among patch tokens.
CONTROLS: Vary the router input between the token feature alone, the token feature plus position, and the token feature plus pooled neighbours while the expert count is held fixed. Compare expert counts of 8, 16 and 32 with the activated parameters held fixed. Measure expert-assignment entropy per layer on identical validation latents. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Expect patch tokens to show far higher mutual similarity than word tokens, and pooled-neighbour routing to yield sharper expert assignment. The claim fails if assignment entropy is unchanged across router inputs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training recipe study for a sixteen-expert diffusion transformer
PROPOSAL: Train a diffusion transformer with sixteen experts whose router reads a neighbourhood-pooled patch feature, and study which recipe choices matter. ImageNet latents at 256 resolution are used with AdamW and a batch of 256. The study also embeds ImageNet patch tokens from a DiT-B and word tokens from a language model and records pairwise cosine similarity at each layer. FID on 50000 samples is reported and related to the similarity measured among patch tokens.
CONTROLS: Vary the data augmentation between flip alone, flip plus crop shift, and flip plus colour jitter while the expert count is held fixed. Compare EMA decay values of 0.99 and 0.999 with the activated parameters held fixed. Measure gradient norm per layer on identical validation latents. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Expect patch tokens to show far higher mutual similarity than word tokens, and the pooled-neighbour router to yield better FID. The claim fails if gradient norms are unchanged across augmentations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling the routing design across model scale and expert count
PROPOSAL: Test whether the gain persists as capacity grows, in a large-scale setting. Train DiT-S, DiT-B and DiT-L backbones and their mixture-of-experts counterparts with 8, 16 and 32 experts, using a router that sees the token feature plus the timestep embedding. Each model trains for 400000 steps on ImageNet latents at 256 resolution with AdamW and a batch of 256, and FID is reported on 50000 samples drawn with one sampler. Fit a power law of FID against activated parameters for every family.
CONTROLS: Compare against the dense counterpart at the S, B and L model scales with matched activated parameters. Add experts from 8 to 16 to 32 while the activated parameters are held fixed. Evaluate FID on 50000 samples with the same sampler at 256 resolution. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Expect the gap to dense models to hold or widen from S to L and with more experts. The claim fails if the fitted power-law exponent of the sparse family is not steeper than that of the dense family.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Early-training behaviour of an eight-expert diffusion transformer
PROPOSAL: Study whether the routing design helps in a short-training setting. Train a DiT-B backbone and an eight-expert counterpart for 10000, 20000 and 40000 steps on nested subsets of ImageNet latents, using a router that sees the token feature plus the timestep embedding. AdamW, a batch of 256 and 64 resolution are used throughout, and FID is reported on 50000 samples drawn with one sampler. Fit a curve of FID against training steps for each family.
CONTROLS: Compare against the dense counterpart at the 10000, 20000 and 40000 step checkpoints with matched activated parameters. Add training images from 10 to 25 to 50 percent of ImageNet while the activated parameters are held fixed. Evaluate FID on 50000 samples with the same sampler at 64 resolution. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Expect the sparse model to match or improve on the dense one at every checkpoint. The claim fails if the fitted curve of the sparse family is not steeper than that of the dense family.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Caption-aware routing in a text-to-image mixture-of-experts transformer
PROPOSAL: Train a text-to-image mixture-of-experts DiT with sixteen experts in alternate blocks, where the router receives the patch feature and a pooled caption embedding from a T5-XL encoder. Training uses a 10M-image aesthetic subset of LAION at 256 resolution with AdamW and a batch of 512. Sample images for 30000 COCO captions with one sampler and one guidance scale, then report FID, CLIP score and GenEval accuracy.
CONTROLS: Compare FID on 30000 COCO captions against the dense DiT with the same number of denoising steps. Compare GenEval object and attribute scores against the dense DiT, grouped by caption length. Measure CLIP score between each image and its caption with identical evaluation seeds. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Expect lower FID and higher GenEval accuracy than the dense DiT at the same activated parameters. The claim is refuted if only FID improves while GenEval and CLIP score stay put.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sparse experts for a caption-conditioned latent diffusion transformer
PROPOSAL: Build a caption-conditioned DiT whose alternate blocks hold sixteen experts, with a router fed by the patch feature plus a pooled caption embedding from a T5-XL encoder. Data is a 10M-image aesthetic subset of LAION at 256 resolution, optimised with AdamW and a batch of 512. Generate images for 30000 COCO captions using one sampler and one guidance scale, then report the denoising loss, wall-clock time per step and expert utilisation.
CONTROLS: Compare denoising loss on held-out COCO latents against the dense DiT with the same number of noise levels. Compare wall-clock time per training step against the dense DiT, grouped by caption length. Measure gradient norm at each layer for every caption with identical evaluation seeds. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Expect lower denoising loss than the dense DiT at the same activated parameters. The claim is refuted if the loss improves while step time and gradient norm stay put.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Neighbourhood-grouped routing for experts that specialize on image content
PROPOSAL: Design a router that groups patches by local spatial context before assignment, so that each expert receives coherent clusters of related content. Train a DiT-B backbone with eight experts and top-2 selection on ImageNet latents at 256 resolution, using AdamW, a batch of 256 and a load-balancing term. FID is reported on 50000 samples drawn with one sampler, and the figures visualise, per expert, the image regions it receives.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed router against a standard top-2 token-choice router with the same experts, the same activated parameters and the same training data. Compare the specialization of experts under both routers by clustering the tokens each expert receives. Measure FID for both routers on identical class labels. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Expect clusters that are more coherent under the proposed router and a lower FID than the standard router. The claim fails if the clustering scores of the two routers are indistinguishable across seeds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Load-balance weighting in an eight-expert diffusion transformer
PROPOSAL: Examine how the router behaves in a DiT-B backbone with eight experts and top-2 selection, where patches are grouped by local spatial context before assignment. Training uses ImageNet latents at 256 resolution, AdamW, a batch of 256 and a load-balancing term whose weight is studied. FID is reported on 50000 samples drawn with one sampler, and the image regions received by each expert are visualised.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed router against the same router with a different load-balance weight, with the same experts, the same activated parameters and the same training data. Compare the specialization of experts under both weights by clustering the tokens each expert receives. Measure FID for both weights on identical class labels. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Expect clusters that are more coherent under the proposed weight and a lower FID than the alternative weight. The claim fails if the clustering scores of the two weights are indistinguishable across seeds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spatially pooled router inputs for continuous latent patches
PROPOSAL: We propose that routers fail on image latents because neighbouring patches are near-duplicates with little content each, and we route on a feature pooled over a patch's spatial neighbourhood and the timestep embedding, adding a loss that rewards agreement between adjacent assignments. We train DiT-B/2 and DiT-L/2 with eight experts on ImageNet at 256 resolution with activated parameters equal to dense and measure FID, sFID, spatial coherence of assignments and consistency across timesteps.
CONTROLS: Dense DiT-B/2 and DiT-L/2 retrained, token-choice DiT-MoE, EC-DiT and DiffMoE under the same schedule and sampler, the pooled router without the agreement loss, and a content-free router that assigns coherent spatial blocks at random, with the throughput of each router and the published FID of each baseline listed next to our retrained numbers.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Pooled routing should beat token-choice routing and dense at both sizes, more so at DiT-L/2. If the content-free coherent router does as well, coherence alone suffices and content specialisation is not what matters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a dense diffusion transformer into a sparse mixture for faster sampling
PROPOSAL: We take a trained dense DiT-XL/2 as teacher and distil it into a student DiT-MoE with eight token-choice experts whose activated parameters are a third of the teacher's, matching the teacher's predicted noise at every timestep on ImageNet at 256 resolution, with the aim of keeping the teacher's quality while activating fewer parameters per image. We measure FID, sFID and throughput of the student against the teacher and against a dense DiT-B/2 student of equal activated parameters.
CONTROLS: A dense student distilled identically, a DiT-MoE student trained from scratch without the teacher, the teacher itself, and progressive distillation to fewer sampling steps as an alternative route to speed, with three seeds, the same sampler and guidance, and inference time and memory per image.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The MoE student should come closer to the teacher than the dense student at equal activated parameters. If the from-scratch MoE matches the distilled one, distillation adds nothing beyond its training signal, and the claim fails.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Can a router tell latent patches apart, a routing-consistency study
PROPOSAL: We train DiT-B/2 with eight token-choice experts on ImageNet at 256 resolution and record every patch's expert across layers, timesteps and neighbouring positions. We compute routing entropy, mutual information between expert choice and timestep, position and semantic label, and expert input-set overlap, and we run the identical analysis on a language MoE of similar size trained on text, so that the difference between the two token kinds becomes measurable.
CONTROLS: Dense DiT-B/2 at equal activated parameters, the MoE with a fixed random router, EC-DiT and DiffMoE under the same schedule and sampler, and the language MoE with shuffled token order as a reference for content-free routing, with FID for the image models, three seeds, bootstrap intervals over patches and the inference time of each router.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Image-patch routing should carry most of its information in timestep and position and little in content, unlike text tokens. If the random router matches the learned one in FID, learned routing adds nothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mixture of experts in the text encoder of a text-to-image diffusion system
PROPOSAL: We replace the feed-forward blocks of the text encoder that conditions a DiT-XL/2 with eight token-choice experts, keeping the diffusion backbone dense, and train the pair on a captioned image dataset of twelve million pairs. Since text tokens are discrete and well separated, the experts should specialise as they do in language models, and we measure whether this improves prompt adherence and image quality.
CONTROLS: The same system with a dense text encoder of equal activated parameters, a dense encoder of equal total parameters, and a frozen pretrained text encoder as well as one retrained from scratch, scored by FID on a held-out caption set, a text-image alignment score, a compositional prompt benchmark, and routing entropy of the encoder experts, with three seeds and a caption-shuffled placebo for the alignment score.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The sparse text encoder should improve prompt adherence modestly and leave FID unchanged. If the frozen pretrained encoder wins on both, encoder training is not the bottleneck.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Upcycling a dense DiT with cluster-initialised routers at XL scale
PROPOSAL: We convert the feed-forward blocks of a trained dense DiT-XL/2 into eight experts copied from the dense weights, and initialise the router from k-means centroids of token features recorded from the dense model across timesteps, so that experts begin with distinct input regions. We continue training on ImageNet at 256 resolution at activated parameters equal to dense and track the overlap of expert input sets, assignment consistency across timesteps and FID over training to see whether the partition persists and pays.
CONTROLS: Upcycling with a randomly initialised router, the dense model continued for the same steps, DiT-MoE and EC-DiT trained from scratch for equal total samples, and centroids computed on shuffled features as a placebo, with the same sampler and guidance, three seeds for the two upcycled variants, and memory and loss curves for each.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Cluster-initialised routers should keep their partition and beat the dense continuation, while random routers should drift to uniform assignments. If the shuffled placebo does equally well, the initial partition is irrelevant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Token caching across timesteps to cut computation in diffusion transformers
PROPOSAL: We reduce the activated computation of a dense DiT-XL/2 by caching the feed-forward outputs of tokens whose features change little between consecutive timesteps and reusing them, with a learned per-token gate that decides when to recompute, trained on ImageNet at 256 resolution. The gate is supervised to keep the output within a tolerance of the full model, and we evaluate how much computation can be skipped without hurting FID.
CONTROLS: The full dense model, a fixed-rate caching rule without a learned gate, uniform token dropping at the same skip rate, DiT-MoE retrained at equal activated parameters as a sparse alternative, and step-reduction with a faster sampler, with FID, sFID and measured throughput across three skip rates and three seeds.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The learned gate should skip a large share of token updates at unchanged FID, beating the fixed rule. If uniform dropping does as well, the gate learns nothing useful about token dynamics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Token merging before routing to raise content per routed unit
PROPOSAL: We test whether the small content of each latent patch limits routing by merging similar neighbouring patches into a single routed unit before each MoE layer and splitting the expert output back, in DiT-B/2 with eight experts on ImageNet at 256 resolution at activated parameters equal to dense. We vary the merge ratio and also compare patch sizes of two and four, and we measure routing entropy per unit, mutual information between expert choice and a semantic label, FID and sFID.
CONTROLS: Dense DiT-B/2 at each patch size, token-choice routing without merging, EC-DiT and DiffMoE under the same schedule, a random router, and a language MoE whose tokens we merge to the same degree, so that the effect of merging is seen on both token kinds, with three seeds and the memory and inference time of each variant.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: Merging should raise semantic mutual information and the gain over dense up to a ratio where resolution loss dominates. If routing entropy does not change with merging, content per unit is not the limiting factor.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sampler and guidance settings for mixture-of-experts diffusion transformers
PROPOSAL: We ask whether existing DiT-MoE models are under-rated because they are sampled with settings tuned for dense models. We take public DiT-MoE and EC-DiT checkpoints and a dense DiT-XL/2 and sweep the sampler family, the number of sampling steps, the guidance scale and the guidance interval, selecting the best setting per model on a validation split and reporting FID, sFID, precision and recall on ImageNet at 256 resolution, so that each model is judged at its own best operating point.
CONTROLS: The settings used in each model's original report, the dense model under the same sweep, a fixed shared setting across all models, and bootstrap intervals over the evaluation set, with the sweep repeated on three seeds of sampling noise and the inference time of each setting recorded.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: Tuned sampling should narrow the gap between MoE and dense models somewhat, with the guidance interval mattering most. If the ranking of models does not change under any setting, sampling is not what holds MoE back.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Two-level routing by noise level then content for diffusion experts
PROPOSAL: We design a router that first assigns each token to an expert group by denoising timestep bucket and then, within the group, to an expert by content, so that content specialisation is learned among tokens of comparable noise. We train DiT-L/2 with sixteen experts in four groups on ImageNet at 256 resolution at activated parameters equal to dense, and measure FID, sFID, expert input-set overlap within and across groups, and assignment consistency across adjacent timesteps.
CONTROLS: Dense DiT-L/2 retrained, token-choice DiT-MoE, EC-DiT and DiffMoE under one schedule and sampler, timestep-only routing with a random content level, content-only routing without groups, and a fixed random router, with three seeds, a single guidance scale, bootstrap intervals over the FID set, and the memory and throughput of each router.
COST: 2600
PREDICTION: Two-level routing should beat both single-level variants and dense on FID, with within-group overlap far lower than across groups. If timestep-only routing with random content does as well, content specialisation contributes nothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mixture-of-experts layers in the latent autoencoder of a diffusion pipeline
PROPOSAL: We place token-choice MoE layers in the decoder of the latent autoencoder that a DiT-XL/2 samples into, with eight experts on the decoder's transformer blocks, and train the autoencoder on ImageNet at 256 resolution with the diffusion model kept fixed. Since the decoder sees nearly clean latents, we expect its tokens to be more separable than noisy diffusion tokens, and we measure whether reconstruction and the final sampled image quality improve at equal activated parameters.
CONTROLS: The dense decoder at equal activated parameters and at equal total parameters, a decoder with experts assigned by random fixed routing, and the original public autoencoder, scored by reconstruction PSNR and a perceptual metric, by FID of samples decoded through each decoder, and by expert input-set overlap, with three seeds.
COST: 2600
PREDICTION: The sparse decoder should improve reconstruction slightly and leave FID of samples nearly unchanged. If the random-routed decoder matches it, the decoder's tokens are no more routable than diffusion tokens.
